deskyard cp: copy files to or from an environment

Usage: deskyard [-e ENV] cp SRC DST

Copies a file or directory between this machine and an environment; write the
environment side as ENV:/path (ENV is an environment on the chosen server, -e
SERVER/… or the default one; an empty ENV, as in :/path, means the chosen
environment). A file lands at DST, or inside DST when it is an existing
directory. A directory's contents land in DST, which is created (like `cp -r
SRC/. DST`). SRC - reads stdin; DST - writes to stdout (a tar stream for a
directory). Files land as user; inside an environment, two local paths are
copied locally.

Arguments:
  SRC        path        required  local path, -, or ENV:/path
  DST        path        required  local path, -, or ENV:/path

Prints: nothing, unless DST is - (the file's bytes or a tar stream)

Examples:
  deskyard cp ./report.pdf alice:/workspace/
  deskyard cp ./site alice:/workspace/site
  deskyard cp alice:/workspace/out.csv .

Where: on the chosen environment (-e ENV); inside an environment without one chosen it acts locally
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error
